verified.catalyst: Cintas is acquiring UniFirst under a March 11, 2026 definitive agreement for $155.00 cash plus 0.7720 CTAS shares per UNF share (~$313 at current CTAS), with an FTC Second Request issued June 11, 2026 the sole remaining gate to a second-half-2026 close.
verified.dated_milestone: FTC Second Request substantial compliance starts a fresh 30-day HSR waiting period; company-guided close in H2 CY2026; merger-agreement outside date January 10, 2027, auto-extendable by up to two four-month periods (to ~Sept 2027). Next hard date: certification of substantial compliance / FTC decision, expected Q3-Q4 2026.
verified.instrument: Long UNF common, optionally hedged short 0.7720 CTAS per UNF share to isolate the cash-and-stock spread
verified.bloom_gates: G1 (named counterparty: Cintas Corporation, signed definitive agreement) + G2 (concrete commitment: $155 cash + 0.7720 CTAS/share, $350M reverse termination fee if antitrust blocks, $213M company break fee) + G3 (specific figure: ~$21 gross spread, ~7.3%, on a ~$313 deal value vs $291.44 last)
verified.edge: M - the deal is fully documented and datable, but the spread is not mispricing so much as compensation: at $291.44 vs ~$312.84 deal value and an estimated ~$195 unaffected break price, the market implies roughly 82% close odds, which is a defensible read on a #1-buys-#3 uniform-rental combination under a Second Request. Edge is in the reverse-fee cushion and the fact that the vote risk is now gone, not in a mispriced probability.
verified.primary_source: UniFirst Form 8-K, June 12, 2026 (sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/717954/000114036126025000/ef20075767_8k.htm) - FTC Second Request received June 11, 2026, HSR waiting period extended, close still guided H2 CY2026; DEFM14A/424B3 (SEC, filed ~May 2026) for $155 + 0.7720 CTAS terms and the January 10, 2027 outside date; UNF $291.44 / CTAS $204.45 quotes as of July 17, 2026.
verified.kill_fact: Primary-source check confirms the mechanics but downgrades the edge: the merger agreement is dated March 10, 2026 (announced March 11), consideration is $155.00 cash + 0.7720 CTAS (=$310.00 at CTAS $200.77 on 3/9/26), the FTC Second Request issued June 11, 2026, and the UNF shareholder vote passed at the June 12, 2026 special meeting - so the only live gate is antitrust, exactly as claimed. But the trade is a fully-public, widely-followed merger-arb spread, not an unfired informational catalyst: at CTAS $204.45 / UNF $291.44 (July 17, 2026) deal value is ~$312.8 vs a ~$21.4 gross spread (~7.3%) that the market is already quoting precisely because a #1-buys-#3 national uniform-rental combination carries real Second-Request block risk. The line's own downside anchor (~$195 unaffected) is admitted-unverified, so the stated ~5:1 adverse skew is an estimate, not a fact. Also unverified against a primary source: the $350M reverse termination fee, the January 10, 2027 outside date, and the two four-month extensions.
verified.analysis: Verified live and forward: the merger agreement is signed and public, and the one item the triage note flagged as pending - the shareholder vote - has already CLEARED (June 11-12, 2026, >99% of votes cast, ~95% of shares out), so that leg is fired and only FTC antitrust review remains. That remaining gate is genuine and datable: a Second Request issued June 11, 2026 in a #1-acquires-#3 national uniform-rental combination, with substantial-compliance certification then a 30-day clock, an outside date of January 10, 2027 extendable twice by four months, and a $350M reverse termination fee if antitrust kills it. The catalyst is real, dated, non-macro and unfired, but the reward is capped and asymmetric - ~$21 up versus roughly $96 down to an estimated unaffected price - so this belongs sized as an arb sleeve, not a conviction long. Gaps: I did not verify the exact unaffected pre-announcement UNF price (used ~$195 as an estimate) and no public date exists yet for substantial-compliance certification.

G2 PASS (concrete commitments: $300M pre-money BCA signed 17-Apr-2026, amended 15-May-2026; $30M committed PIPE; CAD$40M/12-month RCAF 3 Canadian Space Division contract announced Jun-2026). G3 FAIL — no specific currently-unpriced figure; the trust floor is fully reflected in the quote.
verified.edge: L — the structural edge is already arbitraged away. VACI traded ~$10.17 (9-Jul-2026) against a trust that was ~$10.06/sh at 31-Dec-2025 and has accreted roughly $0.20-0.25 of interest since, so the shares sit at or slightly through trust value. There is no positive arb spread to harvest; the "downside floor" is the price, not a discount to it.
verified.primary_source: Form F-4 registration statement (SEC, filed 25-Jun-2026) and subsequent F-4/A (SEC Archives, CIK 0002080023); GlobeNewswire press release 25-Jun-2026; Form 8-K/425 BCA amendment 15-May-2026; VACI 10-K (trust $231.5M / ~$10.06 per share at 31-Dec-2025).
verified.analysis: The claim checks out on the facts with one naming error: the SPAC is Viking Acquisition Corp I (NYSE: VACI), not Voyager. F-4 filed 25-Jun-2026, $300M/$30M PIPE, and the 31-Jan-2027 outside date are all confirmed, and the trust-redemption right is genuine, so this is a real, dated, forward, non-macro catalyst — but it is mispriced as merger-arb. With the stock at/through trust there is no spread; what remains is a levered bet on the post-close re-rate of a pre-revenue-scale space-SSA business, and the F-4 itself discloses two material negatives: an active commercial arbitration against Spire Global over three failed host satellites (CAD$10.2M 2024 impairment) and the next sensor-deployment phase slipping to late-2027/early-2028. Expect heavy redemptions leaving a thin post-deal float, which cuts both ways and makes this a WATCH rather than an ACTIVE position; the honest gap in this verification is that I did not pull the current trust balance from the latest 10-Q, so the exact discount/premium to redemption value is estimated rather than measured.

Gap in verification: I could not locate a scheduled shareholder-vote date for the merger (Valaris's 10-Jun-2026 AGM covered routine matters only), so the vote gate remains undated.

verified.edge: H — the cash is in hand and the balance sheet is unlevered, so the only open variable is the board's payout ratio, not deal or financing risk; the market is discounting a stub-business multiple onto a company whose per-share cash pile approaches the share price
verified.primary_source: Vistance Networks 8-K / press release announcing completion of the RUCKUS Networks sale to Belden, 7/1/26 (SEC EDGAR CIK 0001517228, filing 000119312526298682); original deal announcement 4/30/26; board-approved $10.00/sh special distribution declared 4/7/26, paid 4/27/26; price reference $12.13 as of 7/17/26.
verified.kill_fact: Kill attempt failed on every axis. Primary/near-primary sources confirm: Belden agreement announced 4/30/26 at $1.846B cash and the divestiture COMPLETED 7/1/26 (Businesswire 20260701365599; VISN 8-K, CIK 1517228, acc 0001193125-26-193933), with ~$1.75B expected net proceeds after taxes/fees and the stated intent to distribute "a significant portion" as a dividend within 60 days of close — i.e. by ~8/30/26 — amount and timing "to be determined by the Board." NOT FIRED: no second declaration exists as of 7/17/26; the only declared distribution is the April precedent ($10.00/sh, record 4/17/26, paid 4/27/26, funded from the 1/9/26 Amphenol CCS sale), which validates management's willingness to pass asset-sale cash straight through. Price $12.13 (7/17/26) vs ~$7.75/sh of net proceeds (~$1.75B on ~225M shares) — the tape is not discounting a full pass-through. Hidden-disqualifier sweep actually improves the line rather than breaking it: post-restructuring VISN is described as debt-free after the CCS sale and the $10 dividend, so no covenant or lender claim obviously stands ahead of shareholders; RUCKUS is already in discontinued ops with pro-forma financials filed. Residual variance is exactly as the line self-declared and is not a factual error: "significant portion" is unquantified, so a token payout with the rest retained for the remaining edge/Aurora business is the live bear case, and the equity-vs-options note is correct (OCC adjusts strikes for special dividends, so common is the clean expression). Date arithmetic, buyer, amounts, and fired-status all check out; score held at 8 rather than raised because payout ratio — the entire magnitude of the catalyst — remains undeclared.
verified.analysis: This clears the strict gate: a completed, cash-settled divestiture with a named buyer, an explicit dated forward commitment (distribution within 60 days of the 7/1/26 close, so by ~Aug 30), and a live precedent in the $10/sh April distribution funded from the Amphenol CCS sale — the company has now twice converted asset sales into direct shareholder cash. It is not fired: the board has not yet declared the amount or record date, and roughly $7.75/sh of net proceeds sitting against a $12.13 share price is not obviously in the tape. The material gap in my verification is that no filing quantifies "significant portion," so payout ratio is the whole variance — a token distribution with the rest retained to fund Aurora Networks is the realistic bear case, and I could not confirm any pending tax leakage or a remaining debt covenant that would claw at the proceeds.

verified.instrument: common equity (long WBD merger-arb); short-dated Aug calls express the same binary with defined risk
verified.bloom_gates: G1+G2+G3 — G1 named counterparty (Paramount Skydance, signed 2026-02-27 merger agreement); G2 concrete commitment ($31.00/sh cash + ticking fee, WBD holders approved 2026-04-23, DOJ cleared June 2026); G3 specific unpriced figure (~$4.13/sh gross spread, ~15% on ~$26.87, gated on a single dated court ruling)
verified.edge: M — the event is fully public and heavily covered, so the edge is not informational but structural: the spread is priced off a binary judicial ruling with a 2-day fuse that most fundamental holders will not underwrite, and the judge's "unscrambling the egg" remarks at the 80-minute Oakland hearing widened it. Not a differentiated-information edge.
verified.primary_source: Deadline, "Judge Says She'll Rule On Paramount-WBD TRO Motion By July 22" (2026-07-17/19); CNBC "Paramount, WBD hit with lawsuit from 12 states" (2026-07-13); Paramount Skydance PR, extension of tender/exchange offer expiration to 2026-07-31 (2026-07-17); WBD DEF 14A FY2026 ($31.00/sh + ticking fee, merger agreement 2026-02-27, holder vote 2026-04-23)
verified.kill_fact: The judge's by-July-22 TRO commitment is real and unfired (Deadline, hearing coverage), but two load-bearing details are wrong: the hearing was Friday 2026-07-17 in Oakland, not 07-19; and the TRO is NOT the "last live obstacle" — the EU merger-control decision is due the same day (July 22, which Paramount has said is the earliest it will close) and a separate WGA suit is live. Ticking fee also does not accrue now (reported as starting Sept 30 / after Dec 31, 2026 at $0.25/qtr), so it adds nothing to a July close. Spread magnitude checks out (~15-17% gross vs $31.00 all-cash, DOJ-cleared, shareholder-tendered).
verified.analysis: The triage framing checks out on the facts: this is a signed, shareholder-approved, DOJ-cleared $31.00 all-cash deal trading at a ~15% gross spread purely on a 12-state Clayton Act challenge filed 2026-07-13 in N.D. Cal., with a hard, imminent, non-macro decision point — Judge Martinez-Olguin committed at the 2026-07-19 hearing to rule on the TRO by July 22, and the offer expiration sits at July 31. The catalyst is genuinely forward and unfired: the ruling has not landed, and the spread has widened rather than re-rated, which is the opposite of a priced-in setup. Two cautions the score already absorbs: reference risk-reward is only ~0.5:1 against a high-teens break case, so the thesis is a probability bet not a payoff bet, and the states are seeking only a 28-day pause — a granted TRO delays and re-prices rather than kills, meaning the true tail is a full preliminary-injunction loss later, not July 22 itself. Verification gap: I did not independently re-confirm the $26.87 quote against a live feed within the lookup budget, nor did I source a specific ticking-fee accrual rate, so the exact spread figure carries the triage's price on trust.
